name: kintsugi-mend
title: Kintsugi Mend
description: A panel that survives an error and remembers it: on recovery the shards it broke into spring back with an overshoot, and the crack stays behind as hairline seams — brightest right after the mend, decaying toward --ns-muted and then to nothing over minutes.
useWhen: a panel or widget that auto-recovers (a dropped socket that resynced, a failed fetch a retry resolved) and the fact that it failed should stay legible after the fact, not evaporate with a toast; the crack is anchored to where the failure happened and each seam opens the incident it remembers. Pick transition-panel-crumble instead for a one-way destruction transition with no recovery, or toast-undo-fuse when the feedback is meant to be genuinely ephemeral and undoable rather than a persistent scar.
instruction: Build a wrapper, `KintsugiMend`, that gives an error-recovery cycle a memory instead of letting it evaporate. It takes `children` — the wrapped panel content, which should be presentational (a chart, a status readout, not a component with its own data-fetching side effects): it renders exactly once in the accessible tree, but for the duration of a fracture (`broken`/`mending`) a second, `inert` + `aria-hidden` decorative copy also mounts inside the clipped shard layer purely for the visual break, so any effects inside `children` do run twice while broken — a controlled `status` prop (`"ok" | "error"`), `reason` (default "network error"), `retries` (default 1), `subject` (default "panel", used only in the recovery announcement), an optional `initialIncident` ({reason, retries, recoveredAt}) to hydrate existing history without animating, and a `seed` that fixes the fracture geometry — the same seed always breaks along the same crack, because a scar has a fixed location, not a random one each time. On mount the fracture (3-5 shards) is solved once from `seed` and the measured box size via exact Voronoi cells (half-plane clipping against the rect, O(n^2), pure JS, no canvas): seed points are scattered around a seeded impact point, each cell becomes one shard's clip-path polygon, and the shared cell walls become the crack polylines, each given one deterministic perpendicular jag so a wall reads as a break, not a ruler line. `status` "ok" -> "error" pulls those shards apart along their own centroid-to-center direction (`GAP_PX`, plus a small rotation) on a quick ease-out-expo snap; the wrapped content's real, single, accessible instance is faded out and marked `inert` for the duration (broken content should not be tabbable) while a second, `inert` + `aria-hidden` decorative copy of `children` renders inside the clipped shard layer purely for the fractured look — no interactive control ever exists twice in the accessible tree. `status` "error" -> "ok" is the mend: the shards spring back to identity on a back-eased cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) overshoot, the real content layer reappears and regains focusability, and the moment the shards settle the crack becomes a stack of `<polyline>` seams overlaying the panel, each driven by one shared CSS `@keyframes` (opacity ~0.92 down to ~0.06, stroke crossfading `var(--foreground)` toward `var(--ns-muted)` via `color-mix`) run over a 20-minute `animation-duration` with a per-seam NEGATIVE `animation-delay` seeked to the real elapsed time since that incident's `recoveredAt` — a freshly-resolved incident starts the animation at 0 and a hydrated `initialIncident` seeks straight to its already-decayed frame, so no rAF loop or polling interval ages the scar; the animation is disabled outright under `prefers-reduced-motion` and a JS-computed static equivalent (same opacity/color curve, evaluated from real elapsed time, refreshed by a >=15s interval only while reduced motion is active) takes over — reduced motion skips the shard separate/spring animation entirely (both `separated` toggles happen with `transition: none`) while the seams and the full incident history they carry still render normally, fully legible. Every seam is a real, separately focusable `<button data-kintsugi-seam>` positioned at its jag point, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, whose accessible name states the whole fact as a sentence: "recovered from network error, 2 minutes ago, 3 retries — fracture 2 of 4". Clicking or activating a seam OPENS an incident popover (Geist Mono, `role="dialog"`, labeled `Incident: <reason>`, reason/recovered-time/retry count/session recovery tally as visible text, a Close button) and — critically — a seam click only ever opens, never toggles closed on a repeat click of the same seam; Escape (from anywhere while a popover is open) and an outside pointerdown are the only close paths, both returning focus to the seam that opened it. Recovery announces exactly once via a dedicated `role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` element reading "<subject> recovered after <reason>" — set only on a live error -> ok transition, never on `initialIncident` hydration, since that history was not just witnessed. Colors are --background, --foreground, --ns-muted, --border and --ns-accent (the accent appears only on focus rings, its one legitimate interaction-only use) — the whole effect is a monochrome scar on a near-black surface, explicitly not a gold gradient. Differs from transition-panel-crumble by being a round trip with persistent evidence rather than a one-way destruction transition, and from toast-undo-fuse by anchoring the memory to the exact place the failure happened and keeping it there for the life of the component rather than letting it dismiss itself after a few seconds. Zero dependencies, DOM + SVG + CSS only, no canvas.
